prompt:
You maintain a running summary of a long engineering document that is being read part by part, so that a later reader can model the system in SysML v2 without seeing the earlier parts.
Update the summary with the new part. Keep, as compactly as possible: the full names of system elements, actors and items; every alias or call sign with the full name it stands for; which element produces, sends or receives which item; modes and normative requirements. At most 300 words.

Current summary:
System: Regional Dispatch Center (alias Juniper), continuously operating regional EMS dispatch/coordination point; intake, triage support, ambulance dispatch under approved clinical/jurisdictional protocols; shared picture of incidents, units, access. Jurisdictions own resources/policy. Area divided into response zones (reviewed on road/population/agreement changes); each zone has primary/alternate routes to Emergency Department and Riverside Trauma Center. Intake creates an incident record. Center compares reported conditions with zone coverage, escalates unresolved readiness gaps to operational lead. Actors: - Call Taker Mara (radio alias Larkspur): establishes location first (address, municipality, building/floor/entrance), repeats address, checks landmarks, asks callback number; gathers age, consciousness, breathing, main complaint, symptom onset; distinguishes observed vs reported; notes access barriers; produces Caller Location Correction Slip when address needs clarification; asks follow-ups if location unresolved, updates record; stays on line if info could change priority/access. - Triage Supervisor: assigns/confirms priority, routes to clinical review, coordinates prioritization with dispatch on demand/access changes. - Regional Medical Director: clinical triage policy, protocol limits. - Dispatch personnel: shall apply protocols, seek clinical guidance beyond authority, weigh travel time, restrictions, weather, closures. - Shift Commander (alias Sundial): operational authority, conflicts, surge priorities, escalation, reviews readiness concerns/repositioning; shall not override Medical Director policy or crew on-scene judgment. - Radio Coordinator (alias Mistral): monitors Regional Radio Network; shift-start channel/backup checks. - Paramedic Crew: patient care; shall verify access before constrained routes; reports access barriers/vehicle readiness concerns. - Hospital Liaison Desk (alias Kestrel): receiving capacity/destination constraints. - Emergency Department: receiving considerations. - Fleet Maintenance Cell (alias Bluejay): serviceability/defects; produces Battery Swap Voucher. - Data Quality Officer: reviews dispatch records. Systems: Regional Radio Network; Ambulance Coordination Platform (incidents, assignments, status, zone coverage, unit availability); Computer Aided Dispatch Console (entry, dispatch, validates locations against address/map data; staff verify currency); Ambulance Unit 417; North Gate Status Board (produces North Approach Queue Snapshot); South Gate Status Board (southern access restrictions). Boards checked at shift start and on access changes. Readiness checks shall confirm staffing, comms, supplies, fuel, vehicle condition, maintenance restrictions; reassessed after significant incidents, service interruptions, route/access

New part:
S066: The Hospital Liaison Desk supports intake coordination by confirming facility capabilities and clarifying hospital contact pathways.
S067: The Hospital Liaison Desk checks whether a reported destination preference is compatible with current facility capabilities.
S068: When a facility constraint affects coordination, the Hospital Liaison Desk records the constraint in the incident notes.
S069: The Hospital Liaison Desk produces the Bedside Arrival Receipt when an ambulance arrival has been confirmed.
S070: The Hospital Liaison Desk provides current facility information through established coordination channels without delaying emergency call intake.
S071: The Triage Supervisor reviews incidents when the reported symptoms or uncertainty warrant clinical escalation.
S072: The Data Quality Officer monitors intake records for recurring gaps in location or medical detail.
S073: Call Taker Mara updates the incident record when a caller provides new information before dispatch decisions are finalized.
S074: The Regional Dispatch Center preserves the original caller report alongside subsequent clarifications so responders can distinguish confirmed details from estimates.
S075: Clinical triage begins after Call Taker Mara has captured the caller's reported symptoms, location, and immediate hazards.
S076: The recorded information provides an initial basis for assigning urgency and does not replace clinical reassessment as new information arrives.
S077: Triage Supervisor reviews incidents with uncertain severity, conflicting reports, or signs of rapid deterioration.
S078: Priority is based on the immediacy of threat to life, the likely time sensitivity of care, and the risk of deterioration while awaiting response.
S079: Incidents indicating an immediate threat receive the highest available response priority and prompt dispatch action.
S080: Incidents without an immediate threat are prioritized according to the expected harm from delay and the patient's reported condition.
S081: When essential information is missing, Triage Supervisor directs focused clarification while ensuring that information gathering does not delay an urgent response.
S082: Triage Supervisor escalates clinically ambiguous or unusually severe cases to Regional Medical Director for guidance when time permits.
S083: Regional Medical Director provides clinical policy guidance and does not replace the operational authority responsible for dispatch decisions.
S084: Triage Supervisor sends the Pediatric Acuity Note.
S085: Triage Supervisor is known operationally as Copperfield.
S086: Data Quality Officer is known operationally as Pebble.
S087: Data Quality Officer monitors incident records for missing, inconsistent, or duplicated information that could impair triage or dispatch.
S088: Data Quality Officer sends the Duplicate Incident Audit Memo.

Return JSON {"summary": "..."}.
